(p-100) Surah al-Duha: its purpose

It indicates the night's end, that the most righteous of the righteous, who is the most righteous in an absolute sense, is always in the state of being pleased [with his Lord], and is never separated from it in this world or the Hereafter, because of the attributes of perfection with which he is adorned. These are the attainment of the goal through their spiritual light, like the forenoon (al-duha) with its sensory light, which is the most noble part of the day. From this it is known that its name is the most indicative of its purpose: "In the name of Allah" (bismillah), the Exalter of whomever He wills, the Generous, the Benevolent, the Loving, Possessor of Majesty and Honour; "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahman), whose blessing encompasses the particular and general creation; "the Most Compassionate" (al-Rahim), who raises the people of His love and so singles them out by completing His favour.

* *

When He had decreed, at the end of the night, the felicity of the righteous, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was the most righteous of creation in an absolute sense, and revelation had been cut off from him for a time as a trial for whomever of His servants He willed, and the wellbeing of religion, the world and the Hereafter depended on him (ﷺ), and the two lights (al-malawan) were the cause of [the wellbeing of] the livelihood of creatures and much of their return (to Allah), He, glorified and exalted, swore by them that he (ﷺ) is the happiest of all creatures in this world (p-101) and the next. He began with what suits the state of the most righteous, for whom Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) intended, as a first intention, the light that fills the horizons and erases every darkness that comes back to him and reaches him. Through what He mentioned of the time of bright illumination, the state of the beginning of the day and the end of the night, which is darkness wrapped around its shanks, [the night] that drove the day forward at dawn, He conveyed: ﴿By the forenoon﴾. He mentioned what is most noble and most refined of the day, which is its blossom and its brightest part, its breast. That is the time when the sun is high, because the one for whose sake He swore is the most noble of creatures. This indicates that he attains a nobility that no one else among creation attains.

When he mentioned the day, with its most noble quality, as a fitting match for the one who swears by it, he followed it with the night, qualifying it with what conveys its sincerity, since the most noble aspect of the day has no name specific to it. So He said: ﴿By the night﴾, meaning the night in which the complete good is found. Since the beginning of the night is the end of the day, and the end of the night is the beginning of the day, [light] mixed with the darkness of the dusk, the night is joined to the day. He qualified it with pure darkness, so He said: ﴿when it covers over﴾, meaning its inhabitants have become still, or its darkness has settled, its dimness and blackness have become balanced and pure, so that it covers everything with its darkness. The word al-mutasajji means the one who covers. Along with its covering, its wind became still, so it was at the height of beauty. It is possible that the first [of these] points to what this Messenger ﷺ brings of the muhkam (the clear, definitive verses), and the second points to the mutashabih (the ambiguous verses). These four states of light and darkness, namely light mixed with darkness, [darkness] mixed with light, pure brightness, and pure darkness, which exist in the horizons, have their likeness in the human being. His spirit is pure light, his nature is intense darkness, and his heart is light mixed with the darkness of the self, while the self is darkness mixed with the light of the heart. If the appetite of the self overpowers the luminous quality of the heart, the whole of him becomes dark. If the luminous quality of the heart overpowers the darkness of the self, he becomes luminous. If the spirit prevails over the nature, he is elevated above the rank of the angels. If the nature prevails over the spirit, it lowers him below the rank of the cattle, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in way.﴾ [al-Furqan: 44]

When he swore by this oath, which suits his condition ﷺ, He answered him with His saying, ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾, meaning He has not left you in a way that produces a separation like that of one who bids farewell, even in the best of its forms, which is what the one bidding farewell intends. ﴿Your Lord﴾, meaning the One who showed you kindness by bringing you into existence first, made you the most perfect of creation second, and nurtured you in the finest upbringing third. Just as it is impossible for the night to bid farewell to the day, rather it is the morning (ḍuḥā) that bids farewell to the night, at the moment of its greatest brightness, so it is impossible for the morning to bid farewell to the day, or for the night to bid farewell to it at the time of its stillness (sajw).

Since someone might be obstinate and say, "He did not leave him, but He does not love him," and many a person who keeps in touch is not truly close, He said, negating every kind of abandonment: ﴿nor has He come to hate you﴾, meaning He has not hated you with any hatred at all. The object pronoun was omitted for brevity in wording, so that it would be general. This is reducing the wording to increase the meaning. The reason is that the revelation had ceased from him for a period, because they had asked him about the Spirit, the story of the People of the Cave, and Dhu'l-Qarnayn, and he said, "I will tell you about that tomorrow," and did not say "if God wills." They then said, "His Lord has bidden him farewell and hated him," so this was revealed in response. When it was revealed, he ﷺ exclaimed "Allahu akbar," and so the takbir became a sunnah in it and in what follows, as its explanation and wisdom will come later.

This expression implies that the degrees of nearness are four: nearness through acts of obedience together with love, which belongs to the believers; distancing through sins together with hatred, which belongs to the disbelievers; nearness through acts of obedience mixed with distancing from sins, which belongs to the disobedient believers; and turning away mixed with a semblance of nearness through acts of worship that are not accepted, which belongs to the servants of the disbelievers.

Al-Ustadh (the teacher) Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: When He, the Exalted, said, ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾ [al-Shams: 8], then followed it with His saying regarding the night, ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾ [al-Layl: 7], and His saying, ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾ [al-Layl: 12], and ﴿Indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl: 13], fear became necessary, terror intensified, and it became incumbent upon the monotheist to submit to surrender and to humbly beseech deliverance, seeking refuge with the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Then He, the Exalted, comforted His most beloved servant, the one of greatest rank with Him, and mentioned to him what He had bestowed upon him of nearness and selection, gathering for him the good of both abodes. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 1], ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 2], ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you nor has He hated you﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 3], ﴿and the Hereafter is better for you than the first life﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 4]. Then He enumerated His blessings to him after His generous promise to him with His saying: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 5]. He followed this with His saying: ﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 9], ﴿and as for the one who asks, do not repel him﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 10]. For indeed I sheltered you before you sought it, and I gave you before you asked. So do not meet this with oppression toward the one who approaches you or rebuke toward the one who asks. Far be He, glorified is He, from what He forbade him; rather, this is a reminder of blessings, so that whoever among the community of Muhammad ﷺ is granted success may clarify the path. As for him ﷺ himself, it is enough for you to recognize his mercy and gentleness: ﴿and he was merciful toward the believers﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 43], ﴿Distressing to him is what you suffer; he is anxious over you; toward the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128].

Then reflect on the opening of this surah and the relevance of that purpose. For this reason, the surah before it begins with an oath in the first verse: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1], as an alert to the obscurity of the matter in the conduct expected of the responsible, and the absence of the judgment of outcomes. And to suit this is the condition of one who is reminded by the signs, and what befalls him of fear, since what he is commanded regarding its facilitation and its end is hidden from him; and by seeking refuge in Him, certainty is attained and the degrees of the God-fearing are regarded as small. Then, since this is not entirely hidden from each individual of the responsible, I mean what produces certain knowledge and elevates those fit to ascend in the degrees of the God-fearing, indeed He, glorified is He, may let His chosen servants, through their constancy in piety and reflection, behold the clear path and show them, by direct witnessing and observation, what they had followed before by the hardship of reasoning over evidence. The Prophet ﷺ said to Ḥāritha: "You have found it, so hold fast to it," and he said the same to al-Ṣiddīq. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yūnus: 64]; ﴿Indeed, those who say "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Paradise you were promised"﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 30]; ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 31]. Therefore, for these people, that obscurity no longer remains, nor does the turbidity of their thoughts remain through the thickening of that darkness, because of what God, glorified and exalted is He, has granted them of the blessing of goodness, through what He promised them in His saying: ﴿He will grant you a criterion﴾ [al-Anfāl: 29], and ﴿and He will make for you a light by which you walk﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 28], ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾ [al-An'ām: 122]. So these people acted upon insight, and by the success of their Lord they strove toward great and momentous deeds. They cut off their hopes from the world and prepared for their Hereafter with the clearest of works: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ [al-Sajdah: 16], ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah: 17]. Thus, at the beginning of the matter and the severity of obscurity and darkness, the saying of God, glorified and exalted is He, indicates: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1]; and since the state of one in whose heart faith has been written and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him will eventually lead to a result, the saying of God, glorified and exalted is He, indicates: ﴿And by the day when it becomes manifest﴾ [al-Layl: 2]. And since the paths are confined, though they diverge in My way, ﴿Among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghābun: 2], ﴿a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shūrā: 7], the saying of God, glorified and exalted is He, indicates: ﴿And by He who created the male and the female﴾ [al-Layl: 3], ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 49], ﴿So flee to God﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 50], the One absolutely. So there has become clear to you, if God wills, some of what delights concerning the specification of this oath. And God knows best. As for the surah of al-Ḍuḥā, there is no difficulty in the relevance of opening the oath with the morning, since it gladdens him through what God, glorified is He, does for him, especially when one considers what was mentioned about the occasion of the surah's revelation: that the revelation had slowed down from him until some disbelievers said, "His Lord has hated Muhammad," so the surah was revealed indicating this blessing and good news. — End.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 93, verse 4:

When He mentioned His favour to him in this world, that He would continue to link him to revelation and honour, and that some of this is opened to his community after him, it is narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Did you see what will be opened to my community after me, kufran kufran? That pleased me." When this was the case, and his mention was in a manner that encompassed both abodes, he stated the Hereafter explicitly, as it is higher and more majestic, and (p-107) for the least of those who enter it there is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, so how much more so for what belongs to him (ﷺ). He said, emphasising this just as he had emphasised the first point by an oath, with what they deny: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life)﴾. That is, the Hereafter is the true purpose of existence in itself, because it is lasting and pure, free from the impurities of turbidity; or it is the later state for you, so that it is understood from it that you are continually ascending from one height to a higher one and from one perfection to a more perfect one, forever and without end. He restricted it by saying "for you" because not everyone is like that. ﴿Than the first﴾, that is, the transient world, in which no joy is pure, just as the day that follows the night is better than it and more noble, especially its forenoon. This indicates that people are of four categories: among them are those who have good in both abodes, who are the wealthy people of obedience; [and among them are those who have evil in both, who are the poor disbelievers]; and among them are those who have the appearance of [good in this world and evil in the Hereafter, who are the wealthy disbelievers, and among them are those who have the appearance of evil] in this world and good in the Hereafter, who are the poor believers. Someone has said:

People in this world are of four kinds,
and the soul is bewildered in their reflection.

One whose world is restricted ∗∗∗ for him there is indeed a hereafter after it.

And one whose world is expanded ∗∗∗ for him there is no hereafter after it.

And one who has gathered both his portions ∗∗∗ is blessed in this world and in the Hereafter.

(p-108) And one who falls away from among them ∗∗∗ for him there is neither world nor hereafter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 93, verse 5:

When Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) mentioned the worldly life and the Hereafter, He mentioned what encompasses both of them, of His bounty that He increased for him. So He said, beginning with the particle of initiation (harf al-ibtida') for emphasis of the speech because they deny it, and it is not the particle of oath (lam al-qasam), because when it enters upon the present-tense verb it requires the emphatic nun (al-nun al-mu'akkidah). He joined this lam with the word of deferment (kalimat al-tanfis, i.e., sawfa) to indicate that the giving, even if its time is delayed, is for a wisdom and is certainly going to happen: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you﴾, meaning with a promise that has no breaking of it, even if its time is delayed, by what the particle conveys. ﴿Your Lord﴾, meaning the One who has never ceased to be good to you, with the promise of this world and the promise of the Hereafter. ﴿So you will be well-pleased﴾, meaning that it will follow upon that and be caused by it, your being pleased. This includes what He granted him after the perfection of the self: the perfection of knowledge, the manifestation of the matter, the elevation of the religion, the conquest of lands, the submission of servants, the diminishing of the kingdoms of tyrants, the plundering of the treasures of the Chosroes and the Caesars, and the allotment of spoils, to the point that he would give gifts like one who does not fear poverty. It also includes what Allah the Glorified and Exalted has stored up for him in the Hereafter of the praised station (al-maqam al-mahmud), the well-watered Pool (al-hawd al-mawrud), the Great Intercession (al-shafa'ah al-'uzma), and other things that do not fall under limits. The expression has conveyed that people are of four categories: one who is given and is pleased, one who is withheld from and is not pleased, one who is given and is not pleased, and one who is withheld from and is pleased. It is reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that it is the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an, because the Prophet (ﷺ) will not be pleased with a single one of his ummah in the Fire.

When He promised him that He would continue, every moment, to raise him up through the stages of exaltation and nobility, He reminded him of what He had already raised him to before that, from the time his father died while he was still in the womb and his mother died when he was eight years old. Thus his orphanhood from both parents was completed before he reached maturity, so that, as Ja'far al-Sadiq said, no right of any creature would be upon him. Then He said, affirming this for him: ﴿Did He not find you﴾, i.e., did He not encounter you, meaning: did He not deal with you the way one deals with someone he encounters in a given state, while you were ﴿an orphan, and gave you shelter﴾.

Since orphanhood commonly entails the orphan's lack of knowledge, owing to the neglect of his guardian, and lack of knowledge entails misguidance, (Allah) said, clarifying that his orphanhood and the neglect of him from being pressed into their religion was a great blessing upon him, because he had never at any time been upon the religion of his people at all: ﴿And He found you lost﴾, i.e., He encountered you ﴿lost﴾, i.e., not knowing the sacred laws, ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. So He used the necessary consequence, which is misguidance, to refer to what it entails, and the effect to refer to the cause, which is lack of knowledge. Therefore, for that reason, you would not undertake any of the actions, because you did not know the ruling concerning it except what you knew through sound reason and upright, sound nature, of monotheism and some of its adjuncts. This is taqwa, as was mentioned earlier in al-Fatiha, and it was not intended in its full reality; rather, he was stripped of attachment to any of the sacred laws and the like, by the eliminating of whoever would compel him to that, so that this contemplation would be free for him by himself, and so that by his sound intellect he would arrive at the correct belief in the fundamentals, while abstaining in the subsidiary matters. ﴿And He guided you﴾, i.e., He guided you with a guidance encompassing every knowledge, so your knowledge through revelation, inspiration, and the enabling of reflection is what you did not know.

Since dependents prevent one from devoting oneself fully to knowledge or anything else, He said: ﴿And He found you﴾, meaning while you were ﴿destitute﴾, that is, having dependents whom you could not afford to support generously, or poor. Ibn al-Qattā' said: "ʿāla al-rajul" means he became poor, and "aʿāla" means his dependents became numerous.

﴿And made you rich﴾ through what was provided to you of the profit of trade, then through the acquisition of spoils of war. This implies that people are of four categories: among them are those who found both religion and worldly life; among them are those who lacked both; among them are those who found religion but not worldly life; and among them are those who found worldly life but not religion.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 93, verse 9:

Having reminded him of the favours God had bestowed upon him, these three blessings, He then instructed him as to how he should act in three matching respects. So He said, making this a consequence of what precedes and placing the object of the verb after the fa' for emphasis: ﴿Therefore, as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾, that is, this category (of people), ﴿do not oppress﴾, meaning do not dominate him or prevail over him in anything. For God only made you taste orphanhood so that you would be disciplined with the finest of manners, that you might know the weakness and humiliation of the orphan. And beyond that is his guardianship (kafalah), which is a vicegerency (khilafah) from God, because the orphan has no guardian except God. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the one who sponsors an orphan are like these two," and he pointed with the index finger and the middle finger.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 93, verse 10:

(p-111) When He began with what was the beginning for him, He followed it with what is his end, in that he becomes the head of creation, so that he becomes the place to which men turn with every question, whether of knowledge or of wealth. So He said, placing it first to show His concern for it, indicating that restoring hearts and winning over creation are among the greatest aims in the perfection of the religion: ﴿But as for the one who asks﴾, that is, the one whom poverty or something else has driven to ask, ﴿do not repel him﴾, that is, do not rebuke him with a humiliating rebuke, for the bitterness of poverty is known. Rather, give him, even if it is little, or send him away with gentle words. Likewise the seeker [of knowledge].

When he had mentioned to him the details of how he should treat the orphan, the beggar and the ignorant, He commanded him regarding the knowledge that He had given him, informing him that it is the instrument he would use in the two previous matters and others, because it is the most noble of human states. It is also the most suitable matter to be the conclusion of the surah, so that it corresponds with its opening. He said: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been good to you by setting right everything that concerns you of knowledge and other things, and by the emigration (hijrah) and its beginnings, at the completion of the number of its verses [from] the letter sin, which is eleven. ﴿Then speak of it﴾, that is, mention the prophethood and convey the message. Mention all of His blessings upon you, for they are blessings upon all creation. Among them is His rescuing you by the emigration from the hands of the disbelievers, and His strengthening you with the Helpers. Speaking of them is a way of giving thanks for them, for you are a guide whom people need to follow, and it is incumbent upon them to recognize that for you and to learn your rank, so that they may render you your due. So tell them that I have not forsaken you nor become displeased with you, and whoever says that has failed and lied. Explain to them the details of that by what I have bestowed upon you of knowledge, which is brighter than the brightness of the morning light. Its last part has returned to its first part through the speaking of this oath and that for which the oath was sworn, and what the Most High King has of His abundant grace in that. The Prophet (ﷺ) complied and began this speaking, which expands the breasts, fills the universe with joy, delight and happiness, because it is among the greatest blessings that remove every calamity, by the takbir (saying Allahu akbar), as transmitted in the recitation of Ibn Kathir and in the narration of al-Susi from Abu 'Amr.

The reciters differed regarding its beginning, its end and its wording. Some of them said: it begins from the beginning of Surah al-Duha. Others said: it begins from its end. Others said: it begins from the beginning of al-Sharh. Whoever said it begins with the first (al-Duha) did not say takbir at the end of the surah, and whoever said it begins at the last part ended his takbir with the takbir at the end of it. Its cause was that when Jibril, upon him be peace, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) after the pause in revelation, and recited the surah to him, he said takbir joyfully, because of what had saddened him from the pause and from the words of the polytheists: "his Lord has forsaken him," and in speaking of the blessings that Allah bestowed upon him in this surah, for him and for his community, in compliance with what he had been commanded.

They differed among themselves regarding its wording. Some of them limited it to "Allahu akbar." Others added tahlil (saying "There is no god but Allah") and said: "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest." This is the one in use. Others added "and to Allah be praise." The preferred view is that of the one who said that it is for the end of al-Duha, both in chain of transmission and in meaning. For although the cause was it, and the custom is that whoever is overtaken by a great matter says takbir at its beginning, his preoccupation (ﷺ) with listening to what was being revealed to him prevented him from doing so. When the surah was completed, he became free for it, so that moment was as if it were the beginning of the sudden arrival of that great matter to him. The surah also contains the majestic blessings that call for praise (tahmid, saying "al-hamdu lillah"), and in that there are wondrous artistry that calls for tahlil. The reason for the one who held it to be at the beginning has been made known. As for the one who held it to be for the beginning of al-Sharh, it is because it was at [the end of] al-Duha; so when it is joined with "Alam nashrah," the matter becomes confused. Linking things to their beginnings is the customary matter. Its wisdom, together with what has passed of its cause, is that tahlil is the affirmation of His oneness, exalted and glorified be He, in the matter, and the impossibility of a partner who would prevent Him from anything He wills, of revelation or otherwise. Takbir is singling Him out in greatness, declaring Him free of any taint of deficiency that might befall Him, such as His knowledge of what was not previously known being renewed, which would be a cause for severing the one who was connected to Him by revelation or otherwise. Tahmid is affirming that He alone is perfect, in return for the abundance of His blessings. In that there is an indication that this surah announced that the Qur'an was approaching its close, for the custom of wise administrators is to lighten the stages toward the end for those who travel, as lightening the first stage is out of kindness to those who fall short. Therefore it was fitting that this mention be made at the end, because remembering the ending stirs up such feeling in the wayfarer. And because the shortness of the surahs may perhaps give the impression of something unfitting, the sunnah was to declare Him free (tanzih) by takbir, exalted and glorified be He, above everything that suggests deficiency, and affirming perfection for Him through tawhid alerts to urging contemplation on what this surah contains of gathering meanings despite its brevity, the shortness of its verses and its sweetness, together with what that contains of ease in teaching, training in memorization at the outset, making it beloved and charming, and praising Allah for completing the blessing with the utmost perfection of firm ordering from One who is All-Wise and All-Knowing.
